# Overlabels

> Overlabels turns live stream data (Twitch events, donations, GPS, chat, arbitrary counters) into browser-source overlays for OBS. An overlay is plain HTML + CSS with `[[[tags]]]` in it. The tags resolve against live data and update in real time over WebSockets. There is no JavaScript in an overlay - the template language does the work.
>
> This file is a complete authoring guide. Read it end to end and you can write a working static, alert, or block template without seeing the codebase.

---

## 1. Hard rules - read these first

These are invariants, not style preferences. Violating any one produces a template that silently fails or gets stripped on save.

1. **No JavaScript. Ever.** `<script>`, `javascript:` URIs (including HTML-entity-encoded ones), inline `on*` handlers, `<iframe>`, `<embed>`, `<object>`, `<form>`, `<input>`, `<button>`, `<textarea>`, `<select>` and `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` are stripped on save by the server-side sanitizer. Do not write a template that depends on scripting. If you want behaviour, express it with conditionals, `foreach`, and formatters.
2. **`<audio>`, `<video>` and `<source>` are stripped too.** Not for security - for control. A raw `<audio autoplay>` in template HTML instantiates a fresh element per alert, so rapid-fire alerts stack overlapping playback. Alert sound belongs in the `alert_sound_url` field, which is preloaded and cancels the previous sound when a new alert fires.
3. **Tags resolve exactly once per render.** Substituted values are never re-scanned. If a donor is named `[[[c:foo]]]`, that text renders literally - it does not become a tag. This is the security property that makes user-supplied content safe. Never assume a value can contain a tag that will resolve.
4. **Three fields only:** `head`, `html`, `css`. A legacy `js` column still exists in the database from the first migration, but it is not in the validation rules for creating or updating a template, so nothing can write to it through the app, and no part of the render pipeline reads it. Populating it is not a route to scripting - treat the three fields as the whole surface.
5. **Values are HTML-encoded** on the HTML path. You cannot inject markup through a tag value.
6. **Missing data renders nothing.** No dashes, no "N/A", no invented placeholder. Use `?? default` if you want a fallback.
7. **Overlays never phone home.** A rendered overlay does not send data back to the server.

---

## 2. Template anatomy

Every template has three fields:

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `head` | `<link>` tags for webfonts, `<style>` blocks. No scripts. |
| `html` | The markup, containing `[[[tags]]]`. |
| `css` | Stylesheet. Tags work in here too. |

The rendered page is transparent by default and sized to the OBS browser source. Overlays are added to OBS as a Browser Source pointing at a URL that carries a 64-character access token in the URL **fragment**, so the token never reaches the server.

---

## 3. The three template types

| Type | Lives | Renders | Data it sees |
|---|---|---|---|
| **static** | Always on screen | Continuously, updating live | Twitch channel data, controls, lists |
| **alert** | Fires on an event, then disappears | Once per event, for a set duration | Everything a static sees, **plus `event.*`** |
| **block** | A reusable fragment | Never alone - composed into a static overlay by the Builder | Same as static, but CSS gets scoped |

A **static** overlay is the normal case: a follower goal bar, a chat box, a timer.

An **alert** is bound to one or more events (a follow, a raid, a Ko-fi donation) with a `duration_ms` (default 5000) and `transition_in` / `transition_out` animations. Alerts are designed to fire *inside* a static overlay's DOM so they inherit its CSS, though adding one straight to OBS also works.

A **block** is a self-contained fragment that the Builder places on a CSS grid. Blocks are the composable unit - see §8 for the rules that only apply to them.

---

## 4. Tag syntax

### 4.1 The shapes

```
[[[key]]]
[[[key|formatter]]]
[[[key|formatter:args]]]
[[[key ?? default]]]
[[[key|formatter:args ?? default]]]
```

A key is one or more segments separated by `.` or `:`. It must **start** with a letter, digit or underscore. Hyphens are allowed inside.

### 4.2 Formatters (pipes)

There are exactly 11. An unknown formatter name silently returns the raw value, so typos are invisible - spell them correctly.

| Formatter | Args | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `round` | decimals (default 0) | `[[[c:score\|round:2]]]` |
| `number` | decimals | Locale-aware thousands separators |
| `currency` | ISO 4217 code | Defaults to the user's locale currency. `[[[c:kofi:total\|currency:EUR]]]` |
| `date` | preset or pattern | Presets: `short`, `long`, `date`, `time`. Pattern tokens: `yyyy MM dd HH mm ss` |
| `duration` | pattern | Seconds in, e.g. `hh:mm:ss`, `mm:ss`, `dd:hh:mm:ss`. Units overflow into the largest present unit. No args = smart auto-format |
| `distance` | `km` or `mi` | Input is kilometres. **Without args it returns the raw value** |
| `speed` | `kmh` or `mph` | Input is metres/second. **Without args it returns the raw value** |
| `uppercase` | none | |
| `lowercase` | none | |
| `login` | none | Normalise to a Twitch login (lowercase, strip leading `@`) |
| `mention` | none | Format as `@name` |

All timestamps in Overlabels are **Unix seconds**. Every control has an automatic `_at` companion holding when it last changed.

### 4.3 `?? default`

```
[[[c:kofi:latest_donor ?? nobody yet]]]
```

Three rules that surprise people:

- It fires on **absence only** - null, undefined, or empty string. A present-but-weird value never triggers it.
- The default is emitted **verbatim**. The pipe is **not** applied to it. `[[[x|currency:EUR ?? 0]]]` renders the literal `0`, not `€0.00`.
- It is part of the authored template, so it is never rescanned for tags.
- "Verbatim" means the pipe is skipped, **not** that encoding is skipped. On the HTML path the default is HTML-encoded exactly like a resolved value, so `?? <b>none</b>` renders visible angle brackets, not bold text. On the CSS path nothing is encoded, because a stylesheet is not HTML-parsed. Write defaults as plain text.
- In CSS, a `?? default` anywhere in the stylesheet costs you the fast path - see §6.

### 4.4 Conditionals

```
[[[if:is_live]]]
  LIVE
[[[elseif:c:kofi:donations_received > 10]]]
  Popular today
[[[else]]]
  Offline
[[[endif]]]
```

- Operators: `>=` `<=` `!=` `>` `<` `=`. Note **single `=`** for equality, not `==`.
- A bare key is a boolean test. Falsy: `false`, the strings `"false"` and `"0"`, empty, null.
- If both sides parse as numbers the comparison is numeric; otherwise it is a string comparison, and `> < >= <=` fall back to lexicographic ordering.
- Quotes around the right-hand side are stripped, so `= "live"` and `= live` are the same.
- Nesting works to a depth of **10**.

### 4.5 foreach

```
[[[foreach:c:list:donors as donor]]]
  <li>[[[loop.index]]]. [[[donor]]]</li>
[[[endforeach]]]
```

- `as <alias>` is optional; the alias defaults to `item`.
- Inside the body you get `[[[loop.index]]]` (0-based), `[[[loop.first]]]`, `[[[loop.last]]]`, `[[[loop.count]]]`.
- If items are objects, `[[[alias.field]]]` works.
- `[[[raw]]]` inside a loop dumps the current item as pretty JSON. Use it to discover an unfamiliar shape, then delete it.
- Loops over Twitch collections are capped per user (default caps, max 50) to bound render cost.
- Nesting works, including a `foreach` inside an `if` and vice versa.

**Malformed blocks fail silently.** An unmatched `[[[if:]]]` or `[[[foreach:]]]` aborts processing and leaves raw text on screen. There is no error message. Count your `[[[endif]]]`s.

---

## 5. Available data

### 5.1 Twitch channel tags (static + alert + block)

62 tags, all bare names. The common ones:

```
user_name  user_login  user_avatar  user_created
channel_title  channel_game  channel_followers  channel_delay
followers_total  followers_latest_user_name  followers_latest_date
```

Also `channel_tags_0` through `channel_tags_9`, subscriber and goal collections (iterate them with `foreach`), and `followed_channels`.

### 5.2 Controls - `[[[c:...]]]`

Controls are named values the streamer owns and can change from the dashboard, from chat, or automatically.

```
[[[c:my_counter]]]              own control by key
[[[c:kofi:donations_received]]] service-managed control
[[[c:kofi:total|currency]]]
```

Registered services: `kofi`, `streamlabs`, `fourthwall`, `bmac`, `throne`, `gps`.

Every donation service provisions the same six keys, so swapping the prefix ports a template between
them: `donations_received`, `latest_donor_name`, `latest_donation_amount`, `latest_donation_message`,
`latest_donation_currency`, `total_received`. Ko-fi, StreamLabs and Fourthwall have
exactly those six; Buy Me a Coffee adds `latest_support_type`; Throne adds `latest_item_name`,
`latest_item_thumbnail_url` and `latest_is_surprise_gift`. GPS is a different shape entirely and shares
none of them.

The exact key list per service is generated from the drivers rather than written by hand, so it cannot
drift from the running app: `/help/reference/integration-controls/all-integration-controls`, with one
page per service beside it.

Referencing a service control in a template makes the overlay declare that dependency; if the copier has not connected that service they are warned but not blocked, and it starts working once they connect.

### 5.3 Lists - `[[[c:list:<slug>...]]]`

Lists are realtime ordered collections (raffle entries, a queue, quotes).

| Tag | Gives |
|---|---|
| `[[[c:list:donors]]]` | The whole list as a JSON array string |
| `[[[c:list:donors:json]]]` | Full item objects (`id`, `value`, `added_at`, `label`, `weight`, `color`) |
| `[[[c:list:donors:count]]]` | Item count (`.count` also works) |
| `[[[c:list:donors.0]]]` | Item at index 0 |
| `[[[c:list:donors:first]]]` / `:last` | First / last value |
| `[[[c:list:donors:random]]]` | A random value |
| `[[[c:list:donors:sum]]]` | Numeric sum, `0` when empty |
| `[[[c:list:donors:empty]]]` | `1` when empty, else `0` |
| `[[[c:list:donors:expires_at]]]` | Unix seconds, empty when no expiry |
| `[[[c:list:donors:countdown]]]` | **Live-ticking** seconds until expiry |

**Why index access uses a dot and everything else a colon.** It is not an inconsistency to work
around: numeric indices are dotted (`donors.0`, `donors.1`) because that is the array-index form the
`foreach` machinery materialises against, while colon segments are a namespace of named accessors.
`donors:0` is not a synonym and resolves to nothing. `count` is the one accessor available both ways
(`.count` and `:count`).

`:countdown` combined with `|duration` gives you a working timer with no scripting:

```html
<div class="timer">[[[c:list:raffle:countdown|duration:mm:ss ?? 00:00]]]</div>
```

### 5.4 Event data - `[[[event.*]]]`, alert templates only

Available only while an alert is firing. The set depends on the event type:

```
event.type  event.user_name  event.user_login  event.user_avatar
event.message  event.bits  event.viewers
event.tier  event.tier_display  event.is_gift  event.total  event.cumulative_total
event.from_broadcaster_user_name        (raids)
event.reward.title  event.reward.cost  event.user_input   (channel points)
event.amount.value  event.amount.currency  event.amount.formatted   (donations)
event.top_contributions.0.user_name  event.last_contribution.user_name   (hype train)
```

### 5.5 `event.type` values - read this carefully

**`event.type` is spelled differently depending on where the event came from.** This trips people up constantly.

**Twitch events** carry the raw EventSub subscription type, dotted and prefixed:

```
channel.follow                channel.subscribe
channel.subscription.gift     channel.subscription.message
channel.cheer                 channel.raid
channel.update                channel.channel_points_custom_reward_redemption.add
channel.hype_train.begin      channel.hype_train.progress    channel.hype_train.end
channel.goal.begin            channel.goal.progress          channel.goal.end
channel.poll.begin            channel.poll.progress          channel.poll.end
channel.prediction.begin      channel.prediction.progress
channel.prediction.lock       channel.prediction.end
channel.charity_campaign.donate   channel.charity_campaign.progress
channel.charity_campaign.start    channel.charity_campaign.stop
```

**External services** (Ko-fi, StreamLabs, Fourthwall, BMAC, Throne) carry a normalised type instead:

```
donation   subscription   shop_order   commission
```

So `[[[if:event.type = follow]]]` matches nothing - it must be `channel.follow`. Meanwhile `donation` is correct as-is, and deliberately so: every donation provider normalises to the same word, which is what lets one alert template serve all of them.

```
[[[if:event.type = donation]]]
  [[[event.user_name]]] donated [[[event.amount.formatted]]]
[[[endif]]]
```

`event.source` tells you which service fired it (`twitch`, `kofi`, `streamlabs`, ...), for when you do want to distinguish.

### 5.6 The right-hand side of a condition is always a literal

There is no tag-to-tag comparison. `[[[if:channel_followers >= c:follower_goal]]]` compares the follower count against the literal string `c:follower_goal` and will not do what you want. Compare against a constant:

```
[[[if:channel_followers >= 1000]]]
```

If you need a dynamic comparison, compute it upstream into a single control (Expression Controls do this) and test that control instead.

---

## 6. Writing a STATIC template

A follower goal bar. Note there is no JavaScript anywhere.

**head**
```html
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@600&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
```

**html**
```html
<div class="goal">
  <div class="goal__label">
    [[[channel_followers|number]]] / [[[c:follower_goal ?? 1000]]] followers
  </div>
  <div class="goal__track">
    <div class="goal__fill"></div>
  </div>
  [[[if:c:goal_percent >= 100]]]
    <div class="goal__done">Goal reached</div>
  [[[endif]]]
</div>
```

**css**
```css
html, body { margin: 0; background: transparent; }

.goal {
  font-family: Inter, sans-serif;
  color: #fff;
  width: 420px;
}
.goal__track { height: 14px; background: rgba(255,255,255,.15); border-radius: 7px; overflow: hidden; }
.goal__fill {
  height: 100%;
  background: #a970ff;
  /* A tag inside CSS - resolves to a number, then gets a unit glued on.
     Deliberately plain: no `?? default` here. See the performance note. */
  width: [[[c:goal_percent]]]%;
  transition: width .4s ease;
}
```

Tags work in CSS. A tag directly followed by a unit (`]]]%`, `]]]px`, `]]]vh`) is supported and stays
on the fast path - the unit is baked into the value at write time.

**A performance note for CSS specifically.** The renderer has a fast path that compiles CSS tags into
native custom properties once at mount, then updates them without re-parsing the stylesheet. That path
is skipped **for the whole stylesheet** if the CSS contains `[[[if:]]]`, `[[[elseif:]]]`,
`[[[foreach:]]]`, a `?? default`, or a placeholder glued directly to a **preceding** character
(`#[[[hex]]]`). Everything still renders correctly, just less efficiently.

It is one switch for the entire stylesheet, so a single `?? 0` on a rarely-used rule drops your
constantly-updating progress bar onto the slow path too. That is why `width: [[[c:goal_percent]]]%`
above has no default: it is the one value in this template that changes on every follow.

To handle absence without paying that cost, give the **control** a default value instead of writing
`?? ` in CSS - a control that exists always resolves to something, so the fallback never needs to be
in the stylesheet. Keep conditional logic in the HTML, where it is free.

---

## 7. Writing an ALERT template

Alerts render once per event for `duration_ms`, with enter and exit transitions configured outside the template. Write only the thing that appears.

**html**
```html
<div class="alert">
  <img class="alert__avatar" src="[[[event.user_avatar]]]" alt="">
  <div class="alert__body">
    [[[if:event.type = channel.follow]]]
      <strong>[[[event.user_name]]]</strong> just followed
    [[[elseif:event.type = channel.raid]]]
      <strong>[[[event.from_broadcaster_user_name]]]</strong>
      raided with [[[event.viewers|number]]] viewers
    [[[elseif:event.type = channel.cheer]]]
      <strong>[[[event.user_name]]]</strong>
      cheered [[[event.bits|number]]] bits
    [[[elseif:event.type = channel.subscribe]]]
      <strong>[[[event.user_name]]]</strong>
      subscribed at [[[event.tier_display]]]
    [[[elseif:event.type = donation]]]
      <strong>[[[event.user_name]]]</strong>
      tipped [[[event.amount.formatted ?? something nice]]]
    [[[else]]]
      <strong>[[[event.user_name]]]</strong> did a thing
    [[[endif]]]

    [[[if:event.message]]]
      <p class="alert__msg">[[[event.message]]]</p>
    [[[endif]]]
  </div>
</div>
```

Notes:
- Always provide an `[[[else]]]` branch or guard with `[[[if:event.message]]]`, because a field absent for one event type renders as nothing.
- `event.message` is chatter-supplied. It is HTML-encoded automatically and never reparsed, so it is safe to place directly.
- Do not animate entry/exit in your CSS - the transitions are applied by the alert system.

---

## 8. Writing a BLOCK template

Blocks are fragments the Builder drops into a grid cell. Everything above applies, plus four rules that exist only for blocks.

### 8.1 Fill the box

The Builder wraps your block in a grid cell that has a definite width and height. Your block must fill it:

```css
:root { width: 100%; height: 100%; }
```

If you size yourself in pixels you will not fit the cell the user drew.

### 8.2 CSS gets scoped automatically

On compile, every selector in your block's CSS is prefixed with the placement's unique id, so two blocks using `.label` cannot collide.

- `.label` becomes `#blk-a3f .label`
- **`:root`, `html` and `body` are REPLACED by the wrapper**, not prefixed. So `:root { --accent: red }` attaches your custom properties to your own block, and `body { background: #000 }` paints your cell, not the whole page. This is why §8.1 works.

### 8.3 Known scoping limitations

- **`@keyframes` names are NOT renamed.** Two *different* blocks each defining `@keyframes pulse` collide, last one wins. Namespace your animation names: `@keyframes myblock-pulse`.
- **`@font-face` passes through unscoped** - it is global by nature.
- **Write flat CSS.** Native CSS nesting is treated as opaque; only the top-level selector of a nested tree gets scoped.

### 8.4 Design for key sharing

Controls travel with a block when it is placed. If two blocks both use `[[[c:accent_color]]]`, they share one control and stay in sync - which is usually what a user wants. Choose generic key names for things that should sync and specific ones for things that should not.

### 8.5 A complete block

**html**
```html
<div class="chatbox">
  <h2 class="chatbox__title">[[[c:chat_title ?? Recent chat]]]</h2>
  <ul class="chatbox__list">
    [[[foreach:c:list:chat_log as line]]]
      <li class="chatbox__line">[[[line]]]</li>
    [[[endforeach]]]
  </ul>
  [[[if:c:list:chat_log:empty]]]
    <p class="chatbox__quiet">Quiet in here</p>
  [[[endif]]]
</div>
```

**css**
```css
:root { width: 100%; height: 100%; }

.chatbox {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  width: 100%; height: 100%;
  padding: 12px;
  background: rgba(0,0,0,.55);
  border-radius: 10px;
  color: #fff;
  font: 14px/1.4 system-ui, sans-serif;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.chatbox__title { margin: 0 0 8px; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: .06em; text-transform: uppercase; }
.chatbox__list { margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; }
.chatbox__line { padding: 2px 0; animation: chatbox-in .25s ease; }
.chatbox__quiet { opacity: .6; }

/* Namespaced so another block's `in` animation cannot clobber it. */
@keyframes chatbox-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(4px); } }
```

---

## 9. Mistakes to avoid

| Mistake | What happens |
|---|---|
| Using `==` for equality | The condition never parses. Use `=`. |
| `[[[if:event.type = follow]]]` | Matches nothing. Twitch types are dotted: `channel.follow`. |
| Comparing one tag to another | The right-hand side is a literal string, never resolved. See §5.6. |
| Misspelling a formatter | Silently returns the raw, unformatted value. |
| Forgetting `[[[endif]]]` | Processing aborts; raw template text appears on screen. |
| Expecting `?? default` to be formatted | Defaults are emitted verbatim; the pipe is skipped. |
| Adding `<script>` for "just a little" behaviour | Stripped on save. |
| `<audio>` for an alert sound | Stripped on save. Use the `alert_sound_url` field. |
| `?? default` on a hot CSS value | Correct output, but the whole stylesheet drops to the slow path. Default the control instead. |
| `[[[c:list:donors:0]]]` | Indices are dotted: `donors.0`. Colon segments are named accessors. |
| Sizing a block in pixels | It will not fill the grid cell. |
| Generic `@keyframes` names in a block | Collides with other blocks. |
| Expecting a value containing a tag to resolve | Tags resolve once. By design. |
| `distance` / `speed` with no args | Returns the raw number unconverted. Always pass a unit. |

---

## 10. Machine-readable spec

The lexical grammar, the formatter table, block keywords, operators and limits live in one file that both the PHP and TypeScript runtimes read, so they cannot drift:

- `resources/dsl/dsl.json` - the shared spec
- `docs/design/overlabels-dsl-spec.md` - the full specification, including the formal grammar and the record of eight historical divergences between implementations

If you are extending Overlabels rather than authoring a template: never hand-roll a tag regex. Add the shape to `dsl.json` so both runtimes get it at once.

---

## 11. Reading somebody's actual overlay

Everything above teaches the language. If you have been given a specific overlay to work on, you can fetch it whole:

```
https://overlabels.com/overlay/<slug>/public      -> the preview page (HTML)
https://overlabels.com/overlay/<slug>/public.md   -> the same overlay as one markdown document
```

The `.md` form is a complete, self-contained description of that overlay, and one fetch is enough to understand it:

- its `head`, `html` and `css` verbatim - these three fields are the entire overlay, nothing else is rendered
- every **control** it defines: tag, type, label, default value, and whether the source actually references it
- every **integration** it needs connected (Ko-fi, Streamlabs, Fourthwall, Buy Me a Coffee, Throne, GPS) and which tags read from each
- every **List** it reads
- for alerts: the sound, text-to-speech and chat-message configuration, plus how the author wired its triggers
- the live data tags it reads

This is the thing to ask for when someone says "help me with my overlay" and pastes a link. If they give you the bare preview URL, add `.md` yourself.

### Kits

A kit is a bundle of overlays that copy into an account together. Public kits work the same way:

```
https://overlabels.com/kits/<id>.md
```

That returns the kit followed by every overlay in it, each described in full, plus one aggregated list of the integrations the kit needs as a whole. Note that the kit's HTML page requires a login while the `.md` does not, so `.md` is the only kit URL you can fetch.

A kit and the overlays inside it have separate visibility flags. A private overlay inside a public kit is listed by name and type, because copying the kit copies it too, but its source is withheld. The document says how many are withheld before the contents table.

Two caveats worth stating back to the user:

1. **Control values are defaults, not live data.** Values are shown only for controls the overlay defines. Controls belonging to a connected service are described by type and label but carry no value, because those hold live account data (a real donor's name, actual revenue).
2. **Triggers and Lists are not copied.** They belong to the author's account. An alert's trigger list tells you what the markup expects; it does not carry over to whoever copies the overlay.

Only public overlays have a `.md`. A private one returns 404, the same as its preview page.

---

## 12. Links

**Start at `https://overlabels.com/help.md`.** That is the help index as plain markdown, and it links to
every other page. If you want to crawl the documentation, that one URL is the entry point.

**Every help page is fetchable as plain markdown by appending `.md` to its URL.**
`https://overlabels.com/help/conditionals.md` returns the full source with
`Content-Type: text/markdown`, byte-identical to what the HTML page renders. The bare URL is
server-rendered HTML and carries the full prose too, so either works - prefer the `.md` form, which
is the source itself with no navigation around it.

| Page | Markdown |
|---|---|
| **Help index (start here)** | `/help.md` |
| Conditionals, foreach, and the full `event.*` catalogue | `/help/conditionals.md` |
| Formatting pipes and `?? default` | `/help/formatting.md` |
| Controls (all types, presets, control panel) | `/help/controls.md` |
| Expression Controls (the math layer) | `/help/expressions.md` |
| Math engine (waves, modulo, PRNG, timestamp racing) | `/help/math.md` |
| Lists | `/help/lists.md` |
| Lists in realtime (read endpoint + WebSocket) | `/help/lists-realtime.md` |
| Blocks | `/help/blocks.md` |
| The Builder | `/help/builder.md` |
| Overlays vs Alerts | `/help/overlays-vs-alerts.md` |
| Twitch bot index | `/help/bot.md` |
| Bot commands reference | `/help/bot/commands.md` |
| Bot aliases | `/help/bot/aliases.md` |
| For creators (system overview) | `/help/for-creators.md` |
| For designers (handoff guide) | `/help/for-designers.md` |
| Manifesto | `/help/manifesto.md` |
| Why Overlabels | `/help/why-overlabels.md` |
| Why Ko-fi | `/help/why-kofi.md` |
| Free resources | `/help/resources.md` |

**The reference vault is plain server-rendered HTML** and needs no `.md` suffix. Every entry lives at
`/help/reference/{category}/{slug}` and each one is listed individually in `sitemap.xml`. Three of them
describe the machine-readable surfaces themselves:

| Page | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `/help/reference/for-machines/llms-txt` | This file: what is in it, and how to hand it to an assistant |
| `/help/reference/for-machines/markdown-endpoints` | The "append `.md`" convention |

| `/help/reference/integration-controls/all-integration-controls` | Every control each integration provisions, generated from the drivers |

**Two help URLs have no `.md` twin** and will return an app shell if you fetch them:

- `/help/integration-presets` - searchable preset catalogue, rendered live from source data. The same
  information is described in §5.2 above and on `/help/controls.md`.
- `/help/gamejam` - Chat Castle documentation, still a Vue page.

- Overlabels: https://overlabels.com
- Help index (human): https://overlabels.com/help
- This file, explained: https://overlabels.com/help/reference/for-machines/llms-txt
- Full tag catalogue as JSON: https://overlabels.com/help-reference-index.json
